subject: Zonal failover credits and response-window alignment
messages:
From: Rachel Simmons <rachel.simmons@cloudscale.com>

Cc: Mike Patel <mike.patel@cloudscale.com>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA packaging question — zonal failover credits & response windows

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profiling looked promising for our inference peaks. Before we loop procurement in, I wanted to confirm a couple of details on SLA packaging:

- How do you price zonal failover guarantees vs regional standby? Specifically, what does the crediting look like if we lose a single AZ vs a full region?
- We need 2-hour P1 response SLAs during our US business hours (06:00–22:00 PT) but want 24/7 escalation coverage. Can these be represented as separate add-ons (response-window pricing + 24/7 escalation roster)?
- Any flexibility on onboarding credits or a one-off readiness discount for a 12‑month commit?

We have an active PO loop that would like a tightened number to evaluate next week. Attaching our internal SLA expectations summary as a reference.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Simmons
Head of Platform Reliability — CloudScale Inc

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 3 May 2028 12:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA packaging question — zonal failover credits & response windows

Hi Rachel,

Appreciate the clear asks — happy to run numbers. Short answers up front:

- Zonal vs regional: we treat a single AZ failure as a "zonal event" and apply a smaller credit slab compared to a full-region outage. Typical credit for a zonal outage (where automated failover succeeded but impacted capacity) is 5–10% of monthly invoice for the affected model route; full-region failures start at 20% depending on duration.
- Response windows vs escalation roster: yes, we price those separately. You can pick a daytime (06:00–22:00 PT) P1 SLA band and then add 24/7 escalation coverage as an optional retainer (flat monthly fee) or as a blended hourly on-call surcharge.
- Onboarding credit: we can offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 1 month of estimated committed spend for a 12‑month minimum commitment, subject to final T&Cs.

I'm cc'ing Aditya (se) for the failover cost delta and Grace (CS) to confirm handoff and oncall coverage. I'll send a short proposal with two options (zonal add-on vs regional standby) by EOD Monday.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, GTM Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SLA packaging question — zonal failover credits & response windows

Hi all,

Following up with the technical/price delta notes so you have concrete bands to evaluate. High-level summary:

Option A — Zonal failover add-on (recommended if you want lower steady cost):
- Behavior: automatic traffic redistribution to remaining AZs; degraded throughput possible until autoscaler restores capacity.
- Pricing: +8% on per-token bill for routes with prefix caching; credit slab: 5% monthly credit for single-AZ outage >15 minutes, incremental up to 12% for sustained multi-hour zonal degradations.
- Escalation: daytime P1 (06:00–22:00) included in base for this add-on; 24/7 escalation retainer = $6,500/mo (covers oncall escalation path + 2 named engineers).

Option B — Regional standby pool (higher cost, stronger isolation):
- Behavior: warm standby in a different region; failover typically sub-5min for stateless routes, KV rehydration can add latency for stateful sessions.
- Pricing: +25% on committed capacity for standby pool reservation; credit slab: 20% for full-region outage events >5 minutes.
- Escalation: 24/7 included for commitments >= $150k/mo; otherwise retainer applies.

Notes:
- For both options we can structure a blended discount for 12-month prepay; typical range 7–12% depending on commitment size.
- Onboarding credit: one-time, equal to 1 month of committed spend (as Stephanie mentioned).

I've uploaded a quick cost model: zonal-failover-costs.xlsx (shows blended price points vs monthly traffic). Happy to walk through numbers in a 30-min call — I can do Tue/Wed morning PT.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLA packaging question — zonal failover credits & response windows

Thanks, Stephanie and Aditya — that helps a lot. A couple of clarifying points from procurement/legal:

- CloudScale requirement: 99.95% uptime across our primary region for the production model route. We expect credits to cap out at three months' invoice and want a clear formula for partial-hour incidents.
- For response windows: we can accept the 24/7 retainer, but we'd like the daytime P1 SLA (the 2‑hour window) to be contractually required with automatic onboarding of our primary ops contact into the escalation roster.
- Pricing ask: With a 12‑month committed spend of ~$85k/mo, what blended discount can you give if we take Option A + 24/7 retainer? Also request a one-time onboarding credit and a clause to review credits after Q2 usage.

We aim to have final terms to our legal team by end of next week.

-Mike
Mike Patel

Subject: Re: SLA packaging question — zonal failover credits & response windows

Hi Mike — thanks for the clear constraints. Finalizing the proposal here with the specifics you requested. Key points below (proposal doc attached):

- Service level: 99.95% monthly uptime for primary region on the specified model route. Credit calculation: partial-hour incidents prorated to the minute; credit caps at 3x monthly invoice for sustained multi-day outages.
- Option chosen: Option A (zonal failover add-on) + 24/7 escalation retainer.
- Pricing for CloudScale (12-month commit ~ $85k/mo):
  • Zonal add-on: +7% on per-token usage (we absorbed 1% vs standard for this commit)
  • 24/7 escalation retainer: $6,000/mo (includes two named engineers and quarterly runbooks)
  • Blended commitment discount: 10% off base usage rates for the committed routes
- Onboarding: one-time credit equal to 1 month of committed spend applied on first invoice.
- Contract mechanics: automatic onboarding of CloudScale primary ops contact into our escalation roster; review clause after Q2 to re-evaluate credit slabs and usage profile.

Next steps: I can send a DocuSign with these terms and a short SOW for onboarding. If that looks good, we'll include a short annex that enumerates the exact model routes and the incident credit formula.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call if legal needs a walkthrough.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, GTM Solutions — Redwood Inference
